purpose: Separate ATR admission, stop geometry, RR survival and final selection conditioning before attributing any forward effect to volatility.

A.interpretation: When recent structureLow is near support, support*0.98 can bind across most/all of the formal ATR range; ATR then has little or no marginal effect on RR until the structure-ATR branch becomes lower.

B.interpretation: Below crossover, 1.2% breakout floor binds; above crossover, stop widens linearly with ATR and RR falls for fixed target geometry.

layerDefinitions.definition: Candidate has reached the volatility gate under frozen Formal ordering; no ATR decision has yet been applied.
layerDefinitions.exclusions: Rows already rejected by an earlier Formal gate cannot be interpreted as ATR-eligible.

layerDefinitions.falsification: Do not infer opportunity cost from first-failure counts alone.

layerDefinitions.definition: Derive frozen channel-specific entry/stop geometry without changing target or outcome.
Using the PIT-valid target state available at the original decision clock, compute RR and classify RR>=2 survival.
guards: Target-null and low-RR must remain distinct

layerDefinitions.definition: Observe whether the row survives later Formal signal-grade/ranking/quota stages.
layerDefinitions.note: Selection is downstream conditioning and cannot be used as the only sample for volatility-effect inference.

analyticalFindings: B has an implicit ATR sensitivity kink near ~1.85% when close is near breakout; the exact crossover varies with breakout/close ratio.
A can be almost ATR-insensitive across the full 1%-10% gate when structureLow is sufficiently near support and the 2% support stop remains the lower stop.
RR>=2 creates an additional implicit channel- and target-distance-dependent ATR ceiling that is not equal to the explicit 10% ATR gate.
Therefore one global ATR optimum/penalty is structurally misspecified unless channel and stop-binding state are controlled.

primaryComparisons: within-channel continuous atrPercent conditional on stopDistancePct and targetDistancePct
RR-rejected versus same-date matched RR-survivors at similar setup quality where valid

promotionRules: If ATR effect disappears after stopDistance and RR, classify downstream ATR effect as geometry-mediated/redundant.
If ATR retains incremental downside/path information after geometry, keep as risk-context candidate.
If an apparent optimum exists only in one channel/stop-binding state, prohibit a universal threshold.
No ATR gate, stop, RR, sizing or ranking change without Class-C owner approval.

dependencies.technicalContinuity: Required when stock-volatility windows cross corporate-action resets; runtime not yet certified
dependencies.targetProvenance: Must be PIT-valid at original decision clock
